recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Use newer, specific paging issues for future changes to link-relation names or paging best practices rather than modifying this already-applied STU3 clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-13559 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Search-page issue asking that the paging section explicitly identify the links used for paging and how those links work, or at least link to where that was described. Its recorded resolution was to make this point to http.html#paging.
initial_application: The Jira comment records svn 12837. In Git this is d799b4e939f192a781e79887a956e6cbee5bd0b8, '#13559 - note about paging support', which edited source/http.html to clarify search/history paging support, the Bundle-link continuation model, opaque server-supplied links, and optional server state parameters. The current Search _count section points to http.html#paging for returned Bundle links.
additional_context: Current source/search.html also has an explicit Other Links - Paging subsection naming first, last, next, prev, and previous, and links to HTTP paging best practices. Related Applied issue FHIR-42892 about previous versus prev has already been represented on the combined branch by commit 1ee6826f19686f42042534450f8004b70d77fe74. Later Applied issue FHIR-51428 added paging best-practice guidance that is consistent with the current seed conclusion. A 2017 Zulip implementers thread asked how paging should be performed and was answered by pointing to http.html#paging and the opaque server-supplied link rule.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current build source already explains paging links in the HTTP page and the Search page directs implementers to that guidance while also listing common paging link relations.

related_jiras.note: Later Applied Search-page issue clarified previous/prev paging link relation wording and is already represented on the combined branch.
